sentence: This project sets up a computer server that speeds up the analysis of large sets of medical images and sensor data.
This project tests whether a fiber-rich diet, intermittent fasting and probiotics can reduce lung injury by changing how the gut and lungs affect each other.
This project studies whether transposable elements help control human gene expression and cell fate in response to mechanical forces.
This project gives investigators access to instruments and technical help for studying proteins and metabolites in normal and diseased ocular tissues and cells.
This project tests how changing two pathways that drive initial thymus growth affects how fast and how well immune cells recover after thymus tissue implantation.
This project studies a group of gut mucosal cells found near polyps in mouse models of cancer linked to inflammation, to learn what they do.
This project studies how mutations in one enzyme gene cause inborn errors of metabolism and tries to develop a way to treat them.
This project studies how brain regions activated by stress raise nerve activity that affects heart function in rats.
This project uses a spatial multi-omics platform to study how sulfur mustard and lewisite cause inflammation and damage in pig skin.
This project manages a large collection of genomic data aimed at finding the causes of pediatric cancer and congenital anomalies.
This project studies how the capsule of Streptococcus pneumoniae helps the bacteria cross vascular endothelial cells and invade organs.
This project develops a treatment for advanced cancer using B cells with spherical nucleic acids together with another immunotherapy.
This project studies how epigenetic changes in skin stem cells affect wound healing and aging, and tests whether reprogramming them restores function.
This project develops an mRNA vaccine to try to prevent breast cancer that is driven by inherited gene changes.
This project builds genomic resources for sandflies to find the genetic changes behind their resistance to insecticide.
This project studies how food parenting practices vary across time and how they affect what children eat over the long term.
This project develops red voltage biosensors that work with optogenetics to read out the activity of neurons in the brain.
This project measures background parenchymal enhancement on contrast-enhanced mammograms to test whether it can mark breast cancer risk.
This project tests whether angiotensin-receptor blockers let more T cells enter breast tumors and improve the effect of cancer immunotherapy.
